note: Original factual annotations. Event URLs cite dates and claims; coordinates locate the named place approximately, not battlefield boundaries. BC dates use astronomical years (1 BC = 0).

items.title: Two rivals
items.text: Rome and Carthage began their first war over Sicily in 264 BC.

items.title: Carthage
items.text: Carthage was the African maritime power confronting Rome across the central Mediterranean.

items.title: Sicily surrendered
items.text: The peace of 241 BC required Carthage to withdraw from Sicily; this marker locates the island, not the treaty signing.

items.title: Hannibal reaches Italy
items.text: In 218 BC Hannibal crossed the Alps into Italy. This Po-valley anchor deliberately does not choose a disputed Alpine pass.

items.title: Cannae
items.text: Hannibal defeated Roman armies at Cannae in 216 BC.

items.title: Zama region
items.text: Scipio defeated Hannibal in 202 BC. Zama is located only at regional precision; the battlefield is debated.

items.title: Carthage destroyed
items.text: Roman forces destroyed Carthage in 146 BC; this was a later war, not the immediate outcome of Zama.
